themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Describes itself as the "Largest in India and Amongst the top globally" private airport operator, with an "Integrated plus end-to-end capabilities across the entire airport value chain" and a stated 27.3% share of passenger traffic in India in FY26 (footnote: only operational Indian airports in the GAL portfolio in FY26 - DIAL, GHIAL and Mopa).
- Frames the equity as "A Multi-Faceted Investment Opportunity": a UTILITY BUSINESS ("Stable, Regulated Returns", analogy "Power / Water Utility"), a CONSUMER PLATFORM ("Gateway to Premiumization", analogy "High-Street Mall with Captive & Growing Footfall") and a REAL ESTATE PLATFORM ("Unlocking Value from Prime Land", analogy "Urban Commercial Real Estate Developer").
- Moat framed around long concessions: "Long remaining concession period with rated capacity of 400m+ pax positioned to capitalize on robust traffic growth outlook", and "Mature and predictable tariff regime for Aero Revenue driving 'Sustainable Cash Flow Profile'. CP4 Tariff for DIAL has led to significant uptick in Aero Revenue and Profitability".
- Adjacency platform is positioned as "Non-Regulated", "High Revenue Growth Potential", "Less Capital-Intensive Business", able to "Enable Entry Outside GMR Airports" and "Perpetual Business - Going Beyond Life of Existing Airport Concessions".
- In Q1FY27 GAL-operated Indian airports handled 27% of total India passenger traffic (Delhi 20%), with a 36% share of international traffic (Delhi 29%) described as "the highest quarterly share in past 4 years".

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Corporate identity] The company is "GMR Airports Limited (GAL), Formerly known as GMR Airports Infrastructure Limited"; the presentation is filed under SEBI LODR Regulation 30 for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.
- [Ownership] Deck footnotes state the "Agreement to purchase 10% stake from Fraport concluded as per Corporate announcement dated 7 Mar'25" against the Delhi (74%) holding, while the 100% stakes shown for Mopa (Goa) and Bhogapuram are "To change basis equity conversion of NIIF's current investment which is in the form of CCDs and can be converted into equity of up to 49% stake".
- [Regulatory] GHIAL's Multi Year Tariff Proposal for Control Period 4 (1 Apr'26 to 31 Mar'31) is under review by AERA; Bhogapuram's MYTP for CP-1 including a pre-control period (1 Jul'26 to 31 Mar'32) is under review, with AERA having issued an ad-hoc tariff effective from the commercial date of operation until the regular CP-1 tariff is implemented.
- [Regulatory] The State Government of Delhi reduced VAT on ATF from 25% to 7% w.e.f. 16 May'26.
- [Contract scope] GAL will continue to operate Mactan Cebu only as the Technical Services Provider until Dec'26; Bidar is contracted by GHIAL (Hyderabad Airport).
